To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
open charm production during the prethermalization of a gluon plasma depends sensitively on both the initial parton number density and the effective thermalization temperature.
the total charm production in the equilibrating plasma is strongly enhanced by prethermal charm production, which depends on the space-momenta correlation in the initial state.

the prethermal production of charm quark-antiquark pairs during the equilibrating stage of an equilibrizing gluon plasma can significantly enhance the total charm quark production, and that this enhancement depends sensitively on both the initial temperature and the initial parton distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the production of open charm in a thermalized quark gluon plasma, which may be formed in relativistic heavy ion collisions at the BNL Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) or at CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC).
the study of the production of open charm mesons in the early stages of the collision of heavy ions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the enhancement of open charm in the parton plasma phase can reach a factor of 2-3 over the initial gluonic production, and this factor is insensitive to the initial parton distribution, the initial temperature, and the time scale for equilibration of the partons.
, in the absence of a large initial gluon density or a very large effective temperature, prethermal production does not significantly enhance the open charm production over gluon fusion.

, in the case of an initial gluon density of the order of 1 fm ^{-3}, the enhancement is about a factor 3-10, while for a higher initial gluon density the enhancement is about an order of magnitude larger, depending on the effective temperature of the plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the charm production in the parton plasma phase is significantly enhanced over the initial gluongluon scattering.
the charm production in a thermalized parton plasma is not enhanced over that in a pure gluon plasma.

, for the initial parton densities and temperatures that are relevant to heavy ion collisions at RHIC and LHC energies, the prethermal open charm production is small, and that the final thermal charm production is dominated by the late time thermalization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
charm quark production in the early parton plasma phase is not negligible and should be taken into account in the analysis of experimental data.
the prethermal production can be comparable to or even larger than the thermal production in a gluon dominated system, and the prethermal production is sensitive to the initial parton distribution.

the prethermal production can be significant for the total charm yield, and it may even dominate the total charm production in a parton plasma with a low initial temperature.
